name: Toyotamaphimeia
sum: Large Pleistocene gavialid from Japan and Taiwan, named after the princess Toyotama-hime.
wsnote: About 6.3–7.3 m; the first description suggested 8 m.
holotype: Skull found in 1964 at Osaka University, about 430–380 thousand years old.
material: The Osaka skeleton and remains from other Japanese and Taiwanese sites.
biology: The Osaka excavations of 1964 also yielded fossil shellfish, insects and plant remains from the same beds.
author: Aoki 1983
